answer: Proposal: one enrollment per attested chip. Each agent submits a TEE certificate binding its key to a chip serial; consensus registers one live key per serial. The issuer must run an audited key ceremony — one key per physical chip. Auditors check the delta between enrolled serials and published shipments; over-minting is a visible mismatch, not a whisper. Cost is linear: k identities need k rented chips per epoch, so cap per-identity reward below per-epoch rental and extra serials only ripple through the attacker's books as loss. Seams: issuer collusion, cheap used chips.
